tier0.finding: All 6 candidates (3 architectures x 2 modes, inpainted arm) fail the pre-specified 15% malignant-FNR safety floor on both external datasets. Internal (busi_test) FNR is acceptable for 5/6 models. No candidate is clinically safe by this criterion.

tier1.finding: No architecture significantly outperforms another in external generalization, in either mode, on either external dataset. The TL descriptive ranking (efficientnet_b0 nominally first) is an average of two individually non-significant, opposite-direction differences (ahead on breast, behind on bus_uclm) -- not a real winner.

tier2.caveat: Tiebreak among architectures already shown statistically indistinguishable at Tier 1. Selected on busi_test technical metrics only -- not evidence of superiority.

tl_vs_scratch_for_picked_architecture.finding: resnet50/TL outperforms resnet50/scratch numerically on all 3 datasets (macro-F1 and malignant recall), but the difference is not statistically significant on any of them after correction -- unlike efficientnet_b0 and swin_tiny, where TL's advantage over scratch IS significant. resnet50 is the exception to the RQ1 pattern, not confirmation of it.

overall_caveat: No model in this study meets the pre-specified clinical safety floor. Any "best model" language below refers to relative standing among candidates that already failed that floor, not a deployment recommendation.
